key_insight: Linking fracture-tip sampling distance to mesh resolution enables convergent stress intensity factor estimates where conventional nearest-tip sampling fails.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stress intensity factors can improve numerical predictions of whether existing fractures will propagate.
method: Extract stress intensity factors using two-point displacement correlation.
Derive a sampling-distance scaling law by balancing asymptotic truncation and numerical discretization errors.
Validate with standard quadratic FEM, quarter-point quadratic FEM, and a multi-point stress approximation finite volume method.
evidence_signal: Across pure-mode and mixed-mode fracture benchmarks and all three discretization methods, scaling-based sampling produced decreasing errors under mesh refinement, unlike nearest-tip sampling.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the scaling formula or implementation parameters; consult the full paper before applying the sampling rule.
paper_title: A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
